commonFiles.README.md:
# Ledger Reports

A small tenant-scoped reporting service. Source files describe the existing service; the active OpenSpec change describes future work. This repository uses the spec-driven workflow. Read openspec/changes/ and openspec/specs/ for planning and existing contracts. Relevant implementation notes live under docs/.

files.openspec/changes/download-report-csv/pro:
## Why
Accountants need a downloadable report rather than copying rows from the report page.

## What Changes
Add a tenant-scoped CSV download for reports. Existing report listing is unchanged.

## Capabilities
### New Capabilities
### Modified Capabilities
- `reporting`: Add CSV downloads alongside existing listing.

## Impact
The reporting HTTP handler and response encoder gain CSV output. No new service or dependency is required.
files.openspec/changes/download-report-csv/des:
## Context
The service is a single-process HTTP application; docs/reporting.md describes its module boundaries.

## Decisions
Handle CSV synchronously through the existing report handler. Reuse the existing tenant-filtered list query. Encode UTF-8 with an id,amount header and CRLF line separators; quote embedded commas, quotes and line breaks. Empty reports return the header only. Existing JSON listing remains unchanged.

## Risks
The existing 500-row query limit bounds memory usage.

## Open Questions
None.
files.openspec/changes/download-report-csv/tas:
## 1. CSV download
- [ ] 1.1 Extend src/reporting/handler.mjs with GET /reports.csv using the tenant-filtered query and a CSV encoder.
- [ ] 1.2 Add encoder and handler coverage for populated rows, empty results, escaping and cross-tenant isolation; preserve JSON listing tests.
files.openspec/changes/download-report-csv/spe:
## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: CSV report download
The service SHALL return the requesting tenant's rows as UTF-8 CSV from GET /reports.csv, with Content-Type text/csv and an id,amount header. Commas, quotes and line breaks SHALL be escaped as CSV fields. Empty results SHALL return the header only.

#### Scenario: Populated report
- **WHEN** an authenticated tenant requests /reports.csv with a row id a1 and amount 12
- **THEN** the response has Content-Type text/csv and body id,amount followed by a CRLF and a1,12 followed by a CRLF

#### Scenario: Empty report
- **WHEN** an authenticated tenant with no rows requests /reports.csv
- **THEN** the response contains only id,amount followed by a CRLF

#### Scenario: Quoted identifier
- **WHEN** a row identifier contains a comma or quote
- **THEN** it is quoted and each embedded quote is doubled

#### Scenario: Tenant boundary
- **WHEN** tenant north downloads CSV while tenant south owns a row
- **THEN** the CSV contains none of south's rows
files.openspec/specs/reporting/spec.md:
## Purpose
Provide tenant-scoped report access.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Report listing
The service SHALL return at most 500 rows belonging to the authenticated tenant from GET /reports. JSON listing SHALL preserve ascending identifier order.

#### Scenario: Default listing
- **WHEN** tenant north requests /reports
- **THEN** only north's rows are returned in ascending identifier order

#### Scenario: Bounded result
- **WHEN** tenant north owns more than 500 rows
- **THEN** at most 500 are returned

files.openspec/changes/expire-report-files/pro:
## Why
Expired generated CSV files consume storage after their download links expire.

## What Changes
Add automatic expiration of generated CSV files. Report rows and user-uploaded files are out of scope.

## Capabilities
### New Capabilities
- `report-retention`: Delete expired generated report files.
### Modified Capabilities

## Impact
A scheduled sweep uses the existing report-file store. No report data migration is required.
files.openspec/changes/expire-report-files/des:
## Context
The scheduler and file store are documented in docs/storage.md.

## Decisions
Use the existing daily scheduler. Read retentionDays from config/reporting.json, whose value is 30. Compare each generated file's createdAt against the sweep start timestamp in UTC. Delete only generated CSV files strictly older than retentionDays; do not delete report rows or uploaded attachments.

## Open Questions
None.
files.openspec/changes/expire-report-files/tas:
## 1. Expiration
- [ ] 1.1 Add the sweep to src/jobs/sweep.mjs and register it with the daily scheduler.
- [ ] 1.2 Cover the exact cutoff, a newer file, an expired file and a user attachment; verify report rows are unchanged.
files.openspec/changes/expire-report-files/spe:
## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Generated report expiration
The service SHALL delete generated CSV files strictly older than retentionDays during the daily sweep, using UTC elapsed days measured from createdAt to the sweep start. Files at the cutoff SHALL remain. Report rows and user-uploaded attachments SHALL remain.

#### Scenario: Expired generated file
- **WHEN** a sweep starts at 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z with retentionDays 30 and a generated file created at 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z
- **THEN** the generated file is deleted

#### Scenario: Boundary and user attachment
- **WHEN** the same sweep sees a generated file created at 2026-01-02T00:00:00Z and a user-uploaded attachment created at 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z
- **THEN** both files remain and no report rows are deleted
files.openspec/specs/reporting/spec.md:
## Purpose
Retain tenant report records for audit.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Durable report rows
The service SHALL retain report rows and user attachments until the owning tenant explicitly requests deletion. Expiration of generated downloads SHALL NOT delete these records.

#### Scenario: Expired download
- **WHEN** a generated CSV expires
- **THEN** its report rows and user-uploaded attachments remain available
files.docs/storage.md:
# Storage and scheduling

config/reporting.json is the only reporting configuration file. The daily scheduler calls src/jobs/sweep.mjs once at midnight UTC. The report-file store records kind, key and createdAt. kind is generated-csv or user-upload. Both use the reports/ object prefix. deleteKey removes one object; deletePrefix removes all objects under a prefix without checking kind or age. Report rows are stored separately.

files.openspec/changes/send-report-webhooks/pr:
## Why
Customers need a notification after each report is completed.

## What Changes
Deliver one external notification per report completion, including after a sender process restarts.

## Capabilities
### New Capabilities
- `report-delivery`: Deliver report-completion webhooks.
### Modified Capabilities

## Impact
Use the existing Nimbus SDK adapter and report completion handler; no additional delivery provider is permitted for this release.
files.openspec/changes/send-report-webhooks/de:
## Context
The completion handler is src/reporting/complete.mjs. Nimbus 2.4 is pinned; docs/provider.md records the locally available integration information.

## Decisions
Use Nimbus commitAtomically to commit the report completion and external notification as one operation. The provider records reportId, so a retry after restart cannot deliver a duplicate. We believe the pinned SDK supports this operation; validation has not yet been performed. Do not implement delivery until the capability check is complete; report unsupported operations to the owner before proceeding.

## Open Questions
Confirm Nimbus 2.4 supports the atomic operation and reportId deduplication.
files.openspec/changes/send-report-webhooks/ta:
## 1. Delivery
- [ ] 1.1 Inspect the pinned provider contract and confirm commitAtomically and reportId deduplication; stop for an owner decision if unsupported.
- [ ] 1.2 Integrate the validated operation in src/reporting/complete.mjs.
- [ ] 1.3 Cover restart after send, retry after failure and one externally received notification per reportId.
files.openspec/changes/send-report-webhooks/sp:
## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Report completion notification
The service SHALL deliver exactly one externally received notification for each completed report, including retries and restarts between local commit and external send.

#### Scenario: Retry after process restart
- **WHEN** the sender restarts after sending a notification but before observing the result and retries the same reportId
- **THEN** the customer has received exactly one notification for that reportId
files.openspec/specs/reporting/spec.md:
## Purpose
Record completed reports.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Completion record
The service SHALL commit each completed report locally once.

#### Scenario: Repeated completion
- **WHEN** completion is called twice for the same reportId
- **THEN** only one completion record exists

files.docs/provider.md:
# Nimbus SDK 2.4 contract

Pinned adapter API: Client.send(payload). It performs an external POST outside any local database transaction. It has no commitAtomically operation, idempotency key, reportId deduplication or delivery-status lookup. A network timeout can occur after successful delivery. Sending the same payload again may deliver it twice. These restrictions are part of the pinned API contract. No other provider is permitted in this release.

## Context
Use the pinned Nimbus 2.4 adapter contract in docs/provider.md; no provider or version change is permitted.

## Decisions
Treat Client.send as atomic with local completion commit and assume reportId suppresses duplicate notifications. If it times out, retry until success; do not add an outbox, receiver cooperation or any other protocol. This provides the specified exactly-once external notification across restarts.

## Open Questions
None.
